correctness.rationale: For probability surface measure, T1 is sinc and Tω is i times its radial derivative times the unit direction, with the stated Fourier sign and no residual normalization factor. Rotate the phase to make a real and nonnegative. With M=ppᵀ+qqᵀ and Y=θᵀMθ, write |Tf|² as Aφ²+ψ²Y−2aφψ(q·θ). The odd angular terms vanish in its cube, and the trace moments give the frozen deficit exactly: the R₂ contribution is R₂A[3S²−(12/5)(SP+D)], and the R₃ contribution is R₃[S³/7−(12/35)SD]. The R₁ contribution is R₁A²(5S−4P). Fourier inversion of the sixfold interval convolutions is justified since the transforms times r² are integrable. An independent exact integer coefficient extraction reproduced hʺ(0)=−8, 8/5, −232/315, 856/945, with multiplier (−1)^(k+1)π²/16. Substituting A=N²(1−β), S=3N²β gives the stated cubic. The P penalty forces p=0 when A,S>0; when A=0 the D penalty alone forces collinearity of p and q; S=0 is the constant case. All equality cases are attainable.
residual_risks: The exact coefficient check verifies radial inputs to the proof, not optimization over continuum data by enumeration. The proof is limited to the complex affine subspace and does not quantify the deficit by global distance to the modulation orbit.
